findings: Ownership: all eight concepts are owned by grant_award or grant_programme, matching the record grain (one award row; programme label as its own role). No business-owned concept is asserted from the mixed recipient population.

Amount: dyn.grant_award.amount_approved is emitted as decimal with currency=AUD and currency_basis=inferred (field_evidence examples_by_field_and_role['dyn.grant_award.amount_approved@grant_award'] shows qualifiers {currency: AUD, currency_basis: inferred}); the definition and notes explicitly deny that this is business income or publisher-stated currency. No invented scheme or currency is presented as source-stated.

Recipient identity: dyn.grant_award.recipient_name_as_published and dyn.grant_award.recipient_abn are award-level, personal_data=always, and the definitions explicitly refuse to infer legal form, company status or organisation kind from names or ABN presence. RECEIVES_GRANT is declared but explicitly not emitted (validation.relationships contains only AWARDS_GRANT: 111), so no unsupported business recipient edge is claimed.

ABN: transform chain trim/null_if/abn is checksum-validating; validation shows source_present 85, emitted 85, 0 errors, and the proposal states no invalid value was observed rather than claiming a separate invalid-ABN report exists. entity.abn reuse is correctly deferred until recipient resolution.

Programme code: dyn.grant_programme.code is extracted from grant_list by regex '^([^,]+),' with confidence 0.7 and an explicit statement that no label-match guard exists; held-out row 411 ('L, Lord Mayor\u2019s Community Fund \u2013 Northgate') and row 237 ('L, Lord Mayor's Community Fund - Coorparoo') both yield 'L', consistent with the emitted evidence. The unguarded extraction is disclosed, not hidden.

Programme name: kept verbatim with no suffix stripping; the proposal explicitly declines to assert ward/locality meaning for the ' - <suffix>' component, which is the correct conservative reading of held-out rows 237/319/411.

Time: observed_at has no source path and falls back to resource_last_modified/retrieval; the notes state this is not a publisher-stated observation time. No valid_from/valid_to is fabricated from grant_round.

Record id: 'index' is excluded as an export ordinal; the constructed id uses five stable award attributes with no normalisation, and the collision risk and typographic-variant fragmentation are documented as bounded limitations rather than claimed as stable keys.
Validation: 111 records in, 111 with output, 0 refused, 0 value errors, 862 observations; AWARDS_GRANT 111 edges. No contradictory emitted claim is visible in the field evidence.

Unmapped entries for index, grant_list and abn are honest: grant_list is partially mapped (code + name from separate fields) and the combined string is not stored redundantly; abn is mapped after checksum with the drop-on-invalid behaviour stated.
semantic_risks: Programme identity is the verbatim label, so typographic variants (ASCII apostrophe/hyphen in rows 237/319 vs curly apostrophe/en dash in row 411) create distinct grant_programme entities and fragment AWARDS_GRANT edges. This is disclosed and bounded, but downstream consumers must not treat programme refs as canonical.

dyn.grant_programme.code is emitted at confidence 0.7 with no guard that the label after the comma equals the grant field; a mismatched grant_list/grant pair would silently produce a wrong code. Bounded by the stated reduced confidence, but not verified.
Record-id collision for two genuinely distinct awards sharing all five key values is unchecked; no collision was observed in validation, but the risk remains open.

personal_data=always on recipient_name_as_published and recipient_abn conservatively suppresses organisation recipients too (held-out rows 237/319/411 are organisations), losing utility; this is the documented privacy trade-off, not a factual error.
Currency AUD is an inference from publisher jurisdiction, not source-stated; consumers must read currency_basis=inferred and not treat AUD as publisher-asserted.
RECEIVES_GRANT is declared with zero edges; consumers must not expect recipient links until a later resolution pass.
checked_reuse: entity.abn: correctly not reused for the award-level ABN because recipient identity is unresolved; deferred to post-resolution with checksum validation.
entity.legal_name / entity.trading_name: correctly rejected for organisation_recipient, which mixes personal names, organisations and council units.
ext.entity.holder_kind: correctly not emitted, since recipient kind is not source-stated.
ext.financial.total_income / taxable_income / tax_payable / revenue_band: correctly rejected for amount_approved, which is an award amount, not recipient income.
ext.entity.sector_tag / ext.entity.industry_code: correctly rejected for project text and programme group/code, which are award/programme-owned and not business classifications.
ext.establishment.program: correctly rejected for grant programme, since it is a site-delivered programme code, not a funding scheme.
observation.valid_from / valid_to: correctly not populated from grant_round, which is a round label, not a date.
observation.source_record_id: constructed deterministically with documented limitations; 'index' correctly excluded as an unstable ordinal.
observation.licence: CC-BY-4.0 from metadata is recorded; observation.observed_at left null rather than fabricated from retrieval time.
response.rationale: The proposal is an honestly scoped partial mapping of a mixed-recipient grant dataset. Ownership is correct (award- and programme-level only), the amount is not misrepresented as income, currency is explicitly marked inferred, recipient names and ABNs are conservatively treated as personal with no legal-form or company-status inference, and RECEIVES_GRANT is declared but explicitly unemitted. Validation shows 111/111 records with output, 0 value errors and 111 AWARDS_GRANT edges, and held-out rows 237/319/411 are consistent with the emitted evidence (verbatim programme labels, code 'L', checksum-valid ABNs). Remaining risks — verbatim-label programme fragmentation, unguarded code extraction, unchecked record-id collision, inferred currency and conservative privacy suppression — are explicitly bounded and disclosed, not semantic errors. No wrong owner, unsupported legal-name claim, invented scheme/currency or unimplemented guard presented as implemented was found. This is an agent review, not human sign-off.
